# Best RV power station and solar panel combo

**My pick: BLUETTI AC200L + ALLPOWERS SP037 400 W folding panel**, about **$1,123** with the codes below.

- **Power station:** [BLUETTI AC200L](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac200l) is $899, or $854.05 with code AFF5OFF.
- **Solar panel:** [ALLPOWERS SP037 400 W](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-sp037-400w-solar-panel) is $299, or $269.10 with code ALLPOWERS26.

The two are sold by different stores, so you'll check out in two carts. The codes were last tested on 2026-10-21, so confirm them at checkout. ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/answers/best-rv-portable-power-station-solar-panel-combo-2026-comparison-ecoflow-bluetti))

**Why it works for an RV**
- It has 2,048 Wh of LiFePO4 storage (3,000+ cycles) and 2,400 W continuous output. It has a TT-30 RV outlet plus four 120 V outlets.
- It can expand to 8,192 Wh with two B300 batteries.
- It accepts up to 1,200 W of solar at 12–145 V, so the panel's 45.3 V open-circuit voltage is well within range.
- The panel is IP67-rated and comes with MC4→XT60 and DC adapters.

**Downsides**
- The AC200L weighs 28.3 kg (about 62 lb), and the panel is a heavy 18.5 kg for a folding model.
- One 400 W panel is modest for a 2 kWh battery. You can add panels, since the unit takes up to 1,200 W.
- A 13,500 BTU roof AC draws about 1,500 W running and can spike past 3,000 W at startup ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)). That is above the AC200L's 2,400 W rating, so don't count on it starting your roof AC without a soft-start device. It's fine for a fridge, lights, electronics and a microwave.

**If you want more capacity:** the [ALLPOWERS R4000](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh) has 3,456 Wh, 3,600 W at 120 V and an RV outlet. It's $1,499, or $1,319.12 with code EXTRA12. With one SP037 the pair comes to $1,588.22. At 45 kg it suits an RV where it stays put.

**Other options**
- The [BLUETTI Elite 300](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-300) has 3,014 Wh and a TT-30 outlet for $1,199. It can't be expanded, and it was on pre-order when last checked.
- Another review ranks the EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 (4,096 Wh, 4,000 W) as the best all-round RV station, and it could handle a roof AC. My search results had no purchase link or price for it, so I can't point you to a verified listing ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)).

**Caveats on the sources**
- The Dealectric page only covers BLUETTI and ALLPOWERS and says it has no EcoFlow or Jackery records. It also uses affiliate links.
- This pick is not a head-to-head winner against EcoFlow or Jackery. Other guides rate EcoFlow highest for recharge speed and Jackery for polish ([Acquired Sense](https://www.acquiredsense.com/reviews/power-stations.html)).

If you tell me what you want to run (especially whether you need the roof AC) and how many days you'll camp off-grid, I can size it more precisely.
